nodes.summary: For every regular language $L$ over an alphabet, there is a deterministic two-way automaton with finitely many states whose language is exactly $L$.
nodes.title: Regular languages are accepted by two-way deterministic automata

nodes.summary: For every regular language $L$ over an alphabet, there is a nondeterministic two-way automaton with finitely many states that accepts exactly the words of $L$.
nodes.title: Regular languages are accepted by two-way nondeterministic automata

nodes.summary: Every nondeterministic two-way automaton with finitely many states accepts a regular language.
nodes.title: Finite two-way nondeterministic automata accept regular languages

nodes.summary: The language of every deterministic two-way automaton with finitely many states is regular.
nodes.title: Finite two-way deterministic automata accept regular languages

nodes.summary: For every DFA $M$, the deterministic two-way automaton that simulates $M$ by always moving its head one symbol to the right has exactly the language accepted by $M$.
nodes.title: The two-way simulation of a DFA accepts the same language

nodes.summary: The language of a deterministic two-way automaton $A$ is the set of words accepted by $A$ viewed as a nondeterministic two-way automaton: a word $w$ belongs to it when, starting in the start state with the head at the first position of $w$ and following the step function of $A$ (which moves the head one position left, keeps it in place, or moves it one position right, and gets stuck when it is undefined or would…
nodes.title: Language of a deterministic two-way automaton

nodes.summary: For every deterministic two-way automaton $A$ and every word $w$, $w$ belongs to the language of $A$ if and only if $w$ is accepted by $A$ viewed as a nondeterministic two-way automaton.
nodes.title: Membership in the language of a two-way deterministic automaton

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ with transition function $\delta$, this is the deterministic two-way automaton with the same states, start state and accepting states as $M$ which, in state $q$ reading a symbol $a$, goes to state $\delta(q, a)$ and moves its head one symbol to the right.
nodes.title: A DFA as a two-way deterministic automaton

nodes.summary: For every DFA $M$, the deterministic two-way automaton that simulates $M$, viewed as a nondeterministic two-way automaton, equals the nondeterministic two-way automaton obtained by viewing $M$ as an NFA and letting that NFA always move its head one symbol to the right.
nodes.title: The two-way simulation of a DFA agrees with that of its NFA

nodes.summary: A deterministic two-way automaton $A$ is viewed as the nondeterministic two-way automaton with the same states and accepting states, whose only start state is the start state of $A$, and which can go from state $q$ reading a symbol $a$ to state $q'$ with head move $m$ exactly when the step function of $A$ at $q$ and $a$ returns $q'$ and $m$.
nodes.title: A deterministic two-way automaton as a nondeterministic one

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a deterministic two-way automaton, viewed as a nondeterministic two-way automaton. If, on reading the symbol $x$ in state $q$, it has a transition to state $q'$ with head move $m$ and a transition to state $q''$ with head move $m'$, then $m = m'$ and $q' = q''$.
nodes.title: Deterministic two-way automata have unique transitions

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a deterministic two-way automaton, viewed as a nondeterministic two-way automaton. On reading the symbol $x$ in state $q$, it has a transition to state $q'$ with head move $m$ if and only if the transition function of $A$ sends $(q, x)$ to the pair $(q', m)$.
nodes.title: Transition relation of a deterministic two-way automaton

nodes.summary: A deterministic two-way automaton with state set $Q$ over the alphabet $\Sigma$ consists of a partial transition function, which assigns to each state $q \in Q$ and input symbol $a \in \Sigma$ at most one pair of a successor state and a head move (left, stay or right), together with a single start state and a set of accepting states.
nodes.title: Deterministic two-way automaton

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
